requirement:
Each assessment MUST include `instructions` on its first delivered search
result, even when the result has no matches. `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` share
this rule. A failed search leaves the instructions for the first delivered
result. Subsequent searches and continuation pages MUST omit the field.
rationale:
The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.search_accounting.first_result`.

**Instructions on the first delivered result.**
- `src/authoring/searches.rs#mod[tests]/fn[delivered_searches_including_empty_results_need_explicit_completion]` asserts that the first `ripgrep` result has `instructions` equal to the approved `search_accounting.instructions` text.
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_pages_are_accounted_only_when_delivered_and_replay_stays_closed]` asserts the same for the first page of a paginated `ripgrep` search and of a paginated `ast_grep` search.

**First result with no matches.** The searches.rs test runs an empty `ripgrep` search (`absent` pattern) and an empty `ast_grep` search (`absent()` pattern), each on a fresh `ResultPages`. For each one it asserts `matches == []` and that `instructions` is present with the approved text.

**`ripgrep` and `ast_grep` share the rule.** Both tools are exercised in the first-result case, in the paginated pages.rs test and in the empty-result loop of the searches.rs test.

**Failed search.** The searches.rs test first dispatches an invalid `ripgrep` pattern `(` and asserts an error and no outstanding searches. It then asserts that the next successful search carries `instructions`.
- This was only tested with `ripgrep`. The `ast_grep` failure case is not tested, and I did not treat that as a gap. The accounting is shared: `ResultPages::deliver` in pages.rs asks `Searches::needs_instructions`, which returns `!delivered_any`. `deliver` runs only for results that are actually delivered, so a failed search of either tool cannot clear the flag.

**Subsequent searches and continuation pages omit the field.**
- In the searches.rs test, an empty second search and a repeated third search both assert `get("instructions").is_none()`.
- In the pages.rs test, the continuation page from `next_page` asserts no `instructions` for both tools. The replay of the same page token equals that second page, so it also lacks the field.

The assertions compare against the approved text and check absence, so they would catch an implementation that omitted, duplicated, or misplaced the field.
